clue.text: Dancing stable, colder around start of performance? (13, three words)

definitions.text: Dancing stable, colder around start of performance?

indicators.note: one piece sits around another, so the second goes inside the first
letters that are dancing move about and land in a new order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of performance

explanation.surface: A yard of racehorses feels chillier once the show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a ballet company's ensemble is a 'stable' of dancers, and the rearranged letters wrap round P.
explanation.definitionFit: The corps de ballet is the body of ensemble dancers in a company, a group kept together much as a stable keeps a string of horses.

clue.text: Fish, rather plump, passing by

indicators.note: what is passing goes away, so the small word is dropped from the longer one

parts.note: chubby means rather plump
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A fairly fat fish swims past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link here: it is the very pair of letters that leaves the end of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, common in European rivers.

clue.text: Toxic substance secreted by prehistoric insects

indicators.note: something secreted is tucked away out of sight inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Ancient bugs ooze a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a highly poisonous protein extracted from castor-oil seeds.

clue.text: Personification from love poet in non-verse writing mostly I accepted

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: prose is writing that is not verse, here without its last letter
love is nil in tennis scoring, the round letter
Alexander Pope, the eighteenth-century poet
taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: A poet of love, writing in prose, admits that personifying things is his habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Pope, not Poe; the blocks join in order once prose loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosopopeia is the rhetorical figure of personification, giving human voice or form to abstractions or absent persons.

clue.text: Thrill for Jock racket led astray

indicators.note: led astray means taken off the right path, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman feels a thrill as a noisy gang is led off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Jock' marks the word as Scottish; Jock is a nickname for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dindle is a Scots word meaning to tingle or quiver, a thrill running through the body.

clue.text: As a sight to see in Paris, accept line 'Seine's fantastic'? Not I (11, two words)

definitions.text: As a sight to see in Paris

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and wild, so the letters are freely recombined
not I tells us the single letter named must be left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
the river's name, its possessive ending ignored
the letter to be removed from the material

explanation.surface: A Parisian invites us to admire the line 'The Seine is wonderful', modestly disowning it.
explanation.walkthrough: The I comes out of SEINE before the eleven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: En spectacle is French for 'as a spectacle', on show for people to look at, hence the Paris tag.

clue.text: Smashed bust, obscure

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a drinking spree or binge, a noun
third meaning: to hide from view or dazzle, a verb

explanation.surface: A broken statue is hard to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings: drunk, a bout of drinking, and to hide. 'Smashed bust' looks like a damaged sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind serves as slang for intoxicated, as a noun for a drinking bout, and as a verb meaning to conceal or keep from sight.

clue.text: Old spears: a lunge directed catches cadet, one certainly following behind

indicators.note: following behind places the last pieces after what came before
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the other
something directed has been steered and arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cadet
a means one
yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A cadet in an old fencing or jousting drill makes a thrust with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one certainly' looks like a single phrase but is two pieces placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Launcegay is an archaic word for a kind of light lance or spear, so the plural names several of the old weapons.

clue.text: They make settlements creating trouble in records

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to enter something in a ledger is to record it
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Settlers stir up trouble in the official records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail property is to settle it on a fixed line of heirs, so those who do so make legal settlements.

clue.text: Township in short suggests this temporary accommodation

indicators.note: suggests means the abbreviation, said as letter names, points to the word

parts.note: TP is the short form for township; the two letter names said one after the other

explanation.surface: A small town's abbreviation hints at where a traveller might stay for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of skins or bark used by Plains peoples, easily moved and so a non-permanent dwelling.

clue.text: Locks leg after bend

indicators.note: after puts the second item behind the first in the finished word

parts.note: locks of hair
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: Someone's hair is put up and then they bend down to a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a very tight U-shaped turn in a road, named after the shape of the hair clip.

clue.text: Lady that's spare, and not old

parts.note: a spare figure is lean
ne is an archaic word for not

explanation.surface: A woman who is thin and still young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not old' looks like 'young' but means an old word for 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanne is a woman's first name, and crosswords freely clue girls' names as 'lady' or 'girl'.

clue.text: Seat required for dance performance, of course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rump or buttock, a dialect sense
second meaning: a variant spelling of nautch, an Indian dance show
third meaning: slang short for naturally

explanation.surface: You need a chair for the dance show, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings stacked up; the middle one is a variant of nautch, a display by professional Indian dancing girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as the rump of beef, as a form of nautch, and as informal shorthand for naturally.

clue.text: Get a gun and scare bats in plantation crop

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, and crazy letters fall into a new order

parts.note: these letters only, and joining is dropped

explanation.surface: A planter fetches a gun to frighten off the bats in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals, but it is the word for crazy. Only 'a gun' and 'scare' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall grass grown on tropical plantations for the sugar in its stems.

clue.text: Hint isn't in a clue that's half missing, faulty

indicators.note: half missing means two of the four letters of that word are not there
faulty means broken or wrongly put together, so the order changes

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
the word without its first half

explanation.surface: A setter admits a hint is not in the clue because part of it has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, which is to hint at it.

clue.text: One's kept in chest or box (Scottish)

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the bust is the chest
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A single item stored in a trunk or crate in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest or box' looks like two words for the same thing; chest is wordplay, box is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Buist is a Scots word for a box or chest, including a coffin.

clue.text: What's hot often, and available at all times (5, two words)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hot water often comes from a tap

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: hot water usually comes from a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready for use at any time, as beer drawn from a cask is always to hand.

clue.text: Nigel's troubled about outside broadcast that's inferior

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the name are stirred up

parts.note: the name, its 's being 'is'
OB is the abbreviation for outside broadcast

explanation.surface: Nigel is upset by a poor-quality outside broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means of low character or quality, lowly and base, hence inferior.

clue.text: Interior design, one inspired by Dutch look!

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch

indicators.note: what is inspired is breathed in, so the single letter goes inside

parts.note: ecce is Latin for behold or look
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A decorator, inspired by a Dutch style, says 'Look at this!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look!' with its exclamation is the Latin interjection ECCE, as in ecce homo.
explanation.definitionFit: Deccie is an informal short form for decoration, the decorating and furnishing of rooms.

clue.text: One of algae group that invades mid-sea environs

indicators.note: environs are surroundings, so the words around it hold the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An alga spreads out into the middle of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invades' looks like the action of the alga, but it holds the first half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmids are a family of microscopic green freshwater algae, so one desmid is one member of that group.

clue.text: Ventriloquist's prop, about right for making us laugh

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a ventriloquist works with a dummy, a doll
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's dummy is just right for getting laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means oddly amusing, so something droll gets a laugh from us.

clue.text: Headless ghost holding lute, initially it twangs the strings

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off
holding means having something inside it

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost; here without its head

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of lute

explanation.surface: A phantom with no head clutches a lute and plucks its strings.
explanation.walkthrough: SPECTRE loses its S, then L goes in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectre is an old form of plectrum, the small pick used to pluck a stringed instrument.

clue.text: What looms pass yarn through mostly on time

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end of the word

parts.note: to thread is to pass yarn through, minus its last letter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: On a loom, the weaver passes yarn through as time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looms' looks like weaving machines, but it is the verb: what looms is what threatens.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is something menacing that hangs over us, which is to say it looms.

clue.text: Duck during basic education, being caught in 's' for slips

parts.note: the letter s spelt out is ES; this is its first half

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another
being caught in means being held inside

parts.note: the three Rs are the basics of education: reading, writing and arithmetic
a duck is a score of nought in cricket
the third R
the second half of the letter's spelt name

explanation.surface: A batsman out for nought, caught in the slips — a cricketing disaster during school.
explanation.walkthrough: O sits inside RRR, and that goes inside ES, the spelt name of the letter S. In cricket a duck is no score, and slips are fielders near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are small mistakes, and errors are mistakes of any kind.

clue.text: Merkel's brow isn't furrowed when Right gets in

indicators.note: gets in means enters the middle of the other piece
a furrowed surface is creased and ploughed up, so the letters are turned over

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Angela Merkel's forehead stays smooth when the right wing wins seats.
explanation.walkthrough: Merkel is German, so her brow is the German word for forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirn is German for forehead, and Merkel was the German chancellor, so the clue asks for a German word.

clue.text: Loveless tough worked out tantrum in ritualistic crime

indicators.note: loveless means without love, the round letter for nil, which drops out
worked out means rearranged by effort into a new form

parts.note: the word without its O, then rearranged
a gee is a fit of sulks or temper, a Scots word

explanation.surface: A hardman without affection works off his temper through violent rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggee was the robbery and ritual strangling practised by the Thugs of India in the name of the goddess Kali.

clue.text: Cunning dab escapes subject to control

indicators.note: what escapes gets out and away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: something guidable can be steered or controlled
taken as written; these letters leave

explanation.surface: A crafty little fish gets away from those who would manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: A dab is a flatfish, which the surface suggests; here the letters are lifted out of the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Guile is crafty, deceitful cleverness, the noun sense of cunning.

clue.text: Pollen gatherer getting work in southern California

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

indicators.note: getting means taking in or receiving something inside

parts.note: CA is the postal code for California
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A bee finds work collecting pollen in southern California.
explanation.definitionFit: A scopa is the brush of hairs on a bee's leg or abdomen that collects pollen.

clue.text: Hermit community offering minimum of luxurious mystique

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least of it, a single opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of luxurious
an aura is an air of mystique

explanation.surface: Hermits who live together allow themselves only a hint of luxury and some mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A laura was a group of separate hermit cells under one superior in early Eastern monasticism.

clue.text: Deipnosophist's gems appearing regularly in annuals?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A witty diner's best sayings turn up each year in annual collections.
explanation.walkthrough: A deipnosophist is a master of dinner-table conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana are collections of a person's sayings or anecdotes, the gems a clever table-talker produces.

clue.text: Claim fees wrongly for past crimes

indicators.note: wrongly means not in the right way, so the letters are set out of order

parts.note: both words, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone bills dishonestly for offences committed in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' signals an obsolete word rather than crimes done long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefice is an archaic word for an evil deed or enchantment, so the plural means wicked acts of former usage.

clue.text: Rocky outcrop, one overlooking meandering R. Nile

indicators.note: overlooking means standing in front of and above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a meandering river wanders, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: R is short for river; the letters with the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone rock stands above the winding Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlier is an outcrop of older rock wholly surrounded by younger strata, a geological term for an isolated patch of rock.

clue.text: Cooked meal completely over — not a substantial plate

indicators.note: over means turned over, so this word reads backwards
cooked food is altered from its raw state, so the letters change places

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
all means completely, here read backwards

explanation.surface: Dinner is done and only a meagre plate remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like crockery, but it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin plate or layer, as in a gill or bone, so it is a plate of no great thickness.

clue.text: Eating mess with red bananas, Poles are rendered inactive by them?

definitions.text: Poles are rendered inactive by them?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, and crazy letters go into a new order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: Polish diners, made sluggish by a red mess of bananas, flop about.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles are a magnet's two ends, not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagnetiser removes magnetism, leaving a magnet's north and south poles without force.
